summary: Defines the technology-specific information needed when GMPLS signaling is used for SONET and SDH. It also provides minor clarification to RFC 3946. It is a standards-track document.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 4606 extends GMPLS signaling with the fields needed to request SONET and SDH circuits. It defines both signal properties and labels for locating time-slots in a multiplex.

what is the sukl m label
what does transparency mean in gmpls
subtitle: GMPLS signaling fields for requesting SONET and SDH signals and identifying their time-slots.

tldr.problem: Generic GMPLS signaling needs technology-specific values to request SONET and SDH signal sizes, concatenation, and overhead handling.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC defines traffic parameters carried in RSVP-TE objects or a CR-LDP TLV, plus a SUKLM label that identifies a signal's position in the multiplex.
tldr.outcome: RFC 4606 is a Proposed Standard that obsoletes RFC 3946 and is updated by RFC 6344.

today: RFC 4606 is a Proposed Standard that obsoletes RFC 3946 and is updated by RFC 6344.

sections.title: SONET and SDH in GMPLS
sections.content:
GMPLS extends Multiprotocol Label Switching to switching technologies beyond packets, including time-division multiplexing. RFC 4606 supplies details specific to Synchronous Optical Network (SONET) and Synchronous Digital Hierarchy (SDH).

It builds on the general GMPLS signaling rules. SONET and SDH parameters travel in technology-specific traffic objects or TLVs.
sections.plainLanguage: GMPLS can set up paths through several kinds of network equipment. This RFC adds the details it needs to request SONET and SDH paths.

sections.title: The Traffic Parameters
sections.content:
The traffic parameters include Signal Type, RCC, NCC, NVC, Multiplier, Transparency, and Profile. They describe the basic signal and optional transformations such as contiguous or virtual concatenation.

These transformations follow a fixed order: contiguous concatenation, virtual concatenation, transparency, then multiplication. A zero means a transformation is not requested, except that Multiplier cannot be zero and its default value is one.
sections.plainLanguage: The request names a basic signal and may ask to combine or multiply signals or preserve overhead fields. The parameters must be interpreted in the order defined by the RFC.

sections.title: Concatenation and Transparency
sections.content:
RCC indicates supported contiguous-concatenation types, and NCC gives the number of components. NVC gives the number of virtually concatenated signals. A receiver that cannot support the requested values must reject the request.

Transparency requests that specified SONET or SDH overhead fields reach the far end unchanged. Flag 1 selects the Section or Regenerator Section layer; flag 2 selects the Line or Multiplex Section layer. The Profile field has no standard profile in this RFC and should be zero when sent.
sections.plainLanguage: Concatenation fields say how signals are combined. Transparency fields say which overhead information must pass through unchanged.

sections.title: Carrying Parameters in RSVP-TE and CR-LDP
sections.content:
RSVP-TE carries the same SONET/SDH parameter format in SENDER_TSPEC and FLOWSPEC objects. Their class and type values are specified by the RFC, and a node must check whether it and its interfaces can support the requested signal.

CR-LDP carries the parameters in a SONET/SDH Traffic Parameters TLV with type 0x0838. A node that cannot meet the request reports a resource error using the signaling protocol's defined response.
sections.plainLanguage: RSVP-TE and CR-LDP carry the same signal request in different message structures. Each node along the path checks whether it can support that request.

sections.title: The SUKLM Label
sections.content:
SONET and SDH multiplexes form hierarchies of time-slots. The 32-bit SUKLM label identifies a position through fields S, U, K, L, and M; each field selects a level in that hierarchy, and zero marks an unused field.

The label is meaningful only together with the traffic parameters. For contiguous concatenation, one label identifies the lowest occupied time-slot. For virtual concatenation or multiplication, the signaling carries an ordered list of labels.
sections.plainLanguage: The SUKLM label locates a signal by identifying positions at several levels of a multiplex. Read it together with the traffic parameters to know which signal is requested.

sections.title: Examples of Signal Requests
sections.content:
The annex shows how parameter values express signals such as VC-4, virtual concatenation, contiguous concatenation, and transparent STM-16. For example, a VC-4-16c uses Signal Type 6, RCC 1, NCC 16, NVC 0, Multiplier 1, and Transparency 0.

An optional signal type 20 describes a VC-3 that must end in the AU-3 branch. The annex examples illustrate encodings and are not claims about typical signals.
sections.plainLanguage: The examples show how a request's fields describe a signal and its transformations. The optional VC-3 signal type specifies where the signal must end.

fields.name: S
fields.desc: Selects an STS-3 or AUG-1 position.

fields.name: U
fields.desc: Selects an STS-1 SPE or VC-3 position.

fields.name: K
fields.desc: Selects a TUG-3 position within a VC-4.

fields.name: L
fields.desc: Selects a VT Group or TUG-2.

fields.name: M
fields.desc: Selects a VT or VC within the group.
